terms.gloss: a building plot; the ground a house stands or is built on
evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.10.13: pōnendaeque domō quaerenda est ārea prīmum
Cic. Q. fr. 2.5.2: in āream tuam vēnī
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “ground for a house, a building-spot”. Cicero went to his brother’s ārea while the house was going up (Q. fr. 2.5.2–3); the plot of his own house on the Palatine was an ārea too (Att. 4.1.7). Also an open court and a threshing floor.

sources: Lewis & Short: area
Cicero’s letters and Horace’s Epistles checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).

phrases.latin: Ā puerō ut discessī, in āream tuam vēnī. Rēs agēbātur multīs strūctōribus.
phrases.english: When I left the boy, I went on to your building site. The work was going ahead with a crowd of builders.

phrases.latin: pōnendaeque domō quaerenda est ārea prīmum
phrases.english: and first you must look for a plot to set your house on
